subject: Materials Science
title: Work Hardening: Stronger by Deformation
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Work Hardening: Stronger by Deformation.

hook.text: Bend a copper wire back and forth — it gets harder each time until it snaps.

buildup.text: Deformation creates new dislocations — their density increases from millions to billions per square cm.

discovery.text: Dislocations tangle with each other and lock up — making further slip progressively harder.

twist.text: Heat the metal and dislocations annihilate — annealing restores ductility but sacrifices strength.

climax.text: Cold-rolled steel sheets are work-hardened to precise strength levels for car body panels.

punchline.text: Beat a metal and it gets harder — because its own defects block each other.

quiz.question: Why does work hardening increase metal strength?
options: Deformation removes all defects from the crystal
Increasing dislocation density causes dislocations to block each other
Deformation changes the crystal structure entirely
